data.function: P2 report: connector level through a watchdog reset
data.ruling: The refutation stands. The claim is that the connector level through a watchdog reset is "not determined by the datasheet" and that set isolation latches can hold a high line. The mechanism it gives does not apply to a pad in use. Sections 9.3 and 9.7 require software to clear GPIOn.ISO before it uses a pad, and gpio_set_function() clears it. The ISO bits are reset only by the switched-core isolation signal, and a PADS block reset does not reset them. A reset of the PADS block returns a non-isolated pad to its reset state. The watchdog configuration the datasheet documents is the SDK's _watchdog_enable in section 12.9.6.1, which sets every PSM_WDSEL stage except ROSC and XOSC. That includes RESETS, bit 4 of Table 532. The RESETS: RESET register (Table 535) resets to 1 for PADS_BANK0 (bit 9) and IO_BANK0 (bit 6), so both blocks go into reset. The pads then take their register reset values from Table 853: PDE=1, PUE=0, OD=0, IE=0 and ISO=1. Section 9.3 says the IO mux resets to the null function, so the output is high impedance. A GPIO that drove a buffer input high therefore goes high impedance with the pad pull-down of 32 to 86 kΩ (Table 1436, from R1 and not re-read here). The line does not hold high. It holds its level only if firmware leaves those stages out of PSM_WDSEL and RESETS_WDSEL. That comes from the register contents, not from the isolation latches, and it is a firmware choice for R1 and P5. The coprocessor image enables no watchdog yet (IOBoard.md line 221), so V4 and V73 stay open. The connector level therefore follows from the datasheet once the WDSEL settings are fixed, and the claim's reason for "can stay high" is wrong. The finding is about this function's figure, not about the part, so the scope is function. Not established: with POWMAN_WDSEL.RESET_SWCORE set (Table 490, reset value 0, not set by the SDK), the datasheet does not say whether a watchdog reset of the switched core asserts the isolation signal and sets ISO. That path was not read further.
data.evidence: Section 9.7: "when the ISO bit for each pad is set ... the control signals currently presented to that pad are latched"; "The SDK automatically clears the ISO bit when gpio_set_function() is called"; "The ISO control bits are not reset by the PADS register block reset driven by the RESETS control registers: resetting the PADS register block returns non-isolated pads to their reset state, but has no effect on isolated pads." Section 9.3: at reset the pad is high impedance, input disabled and pulled low, and "the IO muxing is reset to the null function, which ensures that the output buffer is high-impedance". Section 12.9.6.1, watchdog.c line 53: hw_set_bits(&psm_hw->wdsel, PSM_WDSEL_BITS & ~(PSM_WDSEL_ROSC_BITS | PSM_WDSEL_XOSC_BITS)). Table 532, PSM WDSEL: bit 4 is RESETS. Table 535, RESETS RESET: PADS_BANK0 (bit 9) and IO_BANK0 (bit 6) reset to 0x1. Table 853, PADS_BANK0 GPIO0: ISO reset 0x1, OD 0x0, IE 0x0, PUE 0x0, PDE 0x1. Table 528: WATCHDOG RESET PSM changes no power state. Table 490, POWMAN WDSEL: RESET_SWCORE, RESET_POWMAN and RESET_POWMAN_ASYNC all reset to 0x0. IOBoard.md line 221: "The image enables none yet".
